_doc: Queue of approved, staged blog posts awaiting their publish date. See scheduled/README.md. Each entry's HTML lives at scheduled/<slug>.html and is moved to blog/<slug>.html on its publishDate by the publish-scheduled GitHub Action. NOTE (corrected S227, 28 Aug 2026): the LinkedIn teaser step in that workflow is DISABLED (if: false, since 76f0bcb on 4 Aug 2026 - the S200 ruling per MIF-128, no standalone link posts). Publishing a post does NOT post to LinkedIn. LinkedIn posting runs separately from scheduled/linkedin-queue.json via linkedin-scheduled.yml. The linkedinTeaser fields below are retained but unused. This line claimed the opposite for 24 days.

queue.title: Everyone likes it and nobody is buying
queue.description: Thirty-one posts, twenty-three verdicts, zero paying customers. My own numbers, and the two questions I should have asked before I called it a demand problem.
queue.linkedinTeaser: Founders: if everyone loves your idea and nobody buys it, here are my own numbers first - fifty-two projects, twenty-three verdicts, eleven people, six who ever looked at the price, nobody paying - and the two questions I should have asked before calling it a demand problem.

queue.title: I wrote a plan I could never have run
queue.description: A complete, 122-line production spec, six weeks old, zero output. The problem wasn't discipline. Every hard input in it was assigned to the one person who is hardest to schedule.
queue.linkedinTeaser: Founders: the plan you wrote months ago and never started probably isn't a discipline problem. Mine is six weeks old, 122 lines, complete - and every hard input in it is assigned to me.

queue.title: Sixty-nine users. One I am allowed to email.
queue.description: I checked the consent flag on my own database this week. Sixty-eight of sixty-nine had said no. Users are not an audience, and the gap between them is where most founders keep their optimism.
queue.linkedinTeaser: Founders: I ran the consent query on my own database this week - sixty-nine users, one of them contactable. Users are not an audience, and the gap between them is where most of us keep our optimism.

queue.title: I do not have a network
queue.description: Four months of a weekly outreach target, never once met. Not discipline. The plan assumed a network I have never had, and nobody checked whether the input existed.
queue.linkedinTeaser: Founders: I set a target of two qualified contacts a week in July. Four months on the count is zero - not because of discipline, but because the plan drew on a network I have never had.
